9 of 12 claims are true but carried no citation at all; all now have a live URL. Three are defective: chicken wrongly attributed to Sakura Curry, allergen pictograms that exist on no menu (claimed twice), and a 'vegan' marketing claim with zero support. gf 'ask' is correct — a 24h shared kitchen running curry udon, fish & chips and a soba-tsuyu curry base cannot go higher.

So the wheat in a tantan bowl is in the TARE, not just the noodle — swapping the noodle does not make a tantan bowl wheat-free. Rewrite around that; it is the fact a celiac actually needs. Every claim was uncited; 8 now have operator-published citations and the evidence for gf 'no' turned out to be far stronger than the record knew (the shop posts an in-store 「グルテンフリー対応してません」 notice, and the allergen chart proves the wheat sits in the tantan tare, not merely the noodle). Four defects: an 'all-wheat-noodle kitchen' that has four noodle types, allium/oriental-vegan labelling transplanted from the Jiyugaoka parent restaurant (claimed twice), a staff-handling line that softens a published refusal into 'not confirmed', and a stale location. Considered and REJECTED a gf upgrade: the rice-noodle wheat-free shio bowl exists only at the Akihabara store, and the operator disclaims gluten-free outright. vegan 'full' is correct.

Unusually good record: 9 of 10 claims are true, several word-for-word matches to the operator's published allergen policy, and all were sitting uncited. One defect — an English/picture menu evidenced only on the sibling Tokyo/Akihabara chart. Trading status confirmed OPEN (ecute 上野 改札内3F, 10:00-22:00). gf 'no' and vegan 'full' both correct. NOTE FOR A HUMAN, NOT A PROMOTION: on the Ueno chart 麺変更（蒟蒻麺）and 麺変更（米粉麺）carry zero allergen marks, and the sibling chart shows the SIO (salt) tare is wheat-free — so a shio bowl with a konjac noodle may be wheat-free at this branch. The operator's own in-store notice says 「グルテンフリー対応してません」, so I am NOT recommending an upgrade; it is a question worth phoning the shop about.
